Around docs#Equiv.Perm.trans_one there are a lot of lemmas that simplify expressions of the form e.symm * e that mix the algebraic and the standard way of writing composition/inversion/identity. This is repeated in some other contexts: docs#LinearIsometryEquiv.trans_one, but not others: docs#LinearIsometry has the definition, but not much else, docs#Homeomorph does not even have some of the definitions.
The braindead way would be copying all of these silly lemmas in every context (would be amazing for saying how many theorems we have in mathlib), but it seems to me that what one really wants is a way move between the two representations and then let simp do the rest. In the case of docs#Equiv this works like a charm: #38359. I have two questions: (a) do people agree with me on the general idea? (b) there is some bikeshedding about the names of the simpsets, they should also be used for maps, so the current names are not good.
